findings.premise: Every approved DEF acceptance criterion (s1–s5, ac1/ac2) is designed in the HLD, the linear s1→s2→s3→s4→s5 order is kept, and no DEF non-goal (project guideline activation, page or framework generation, copying the UI UX Pro Max catalog) is built.
findings.evidence: In DEF-7e0ae92e8f3d3c3e.json the stories depend in a straight line: s2 dependsOn [s1], s3 [s2], s4 [s3], s5 [s4]. The HLD rollout uses the same order ("Matches approved s1→s2→s3→s4→s5"). Each criterion has a matching contract and test. S001/ac1 maps to the sc2 publication gate. S001/ac2 maps to the sc1 identity, relations, rationale and provenance fields. S002/ac1 and ac2 map to sc3 SourceFile and notices. S003/ac1 maps to sc4 CoverageCell across the ten PRD domains (DEF s3/ac1) × three UI types. S003/ac2 is the draft/inferred exclusion. S004/ac1 and ac2 map to sc5 CorpusHit.fit and gaps. S005/ac1 and ac2 map to sc6 withdrawal and pinned EvidenceRef. The non-goals are respected: "DI2 owns project-private guideline storage and DI3 owns authoring workflows", DI3 builds "never page-specific guideline identities", and the HLD stores no project state.

findings.premise: server.ts:187 dispatches the handlers map, and a thrown handler error reaches the client only as a string, so typed domain errors must be returned inside the result.
findings.evidence: server.ts:187 `const handler = this.handlers[request.method];`. Lines 193-197 send `{ id, result }`, and when the handler throws they send `{ id, error: failureMessage(err, request.method) }`. failureMessage (server.ts:71-77) returns `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`, so it is a string. [files: src/daemon/server.ts]

findings.premise: copy-assets.mjs copies src/assets recursively into out/assets, so a new src/assets/design-corpus/ subtree ships with no build change.
findings.evidence: copy-assets.mjs:28 `const DIRS = ['prompts', 'assets'];` and :39 `cpSync(src, dst, { recursive: true });`. [files: copy-assets.mjs]

findings.premise: JetBrains SettingsView.kt has a group order list that needs 'Design intelligence' added to it.
findings.evidence: SettingsView.kt has no hard-coded group list. groupsOf (lines 73-92) iterates `catalog.groups` from the payload, and any group missing from that list is appended in first-seen order. The only group literal is `const val GENERAL_GROUP = "General"` (line 95). On the daemon side, settings-catalog.ts:77-80 builds `groups` in first-seen catalog order from CONFIG_CATALOG. Adding a catalog row with group 'Design intelligence' is enough to make the group render. Following the HLD as written would mean editing code that has no order list, or adding a hard-coded order that cuts against the catalog-driven design. [files: jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/settings/SettingsView.kt, src/config/settings-catalog.ts]
findings.action: Change the s4 JetBrains item to: no SettingsView.kt edit is needed, because the group order comes from CONFIG_CATALOG's first-seen order. Keep only a check that the new boolean renders and round-trips.

findings.premise: src/analyze/docs-retrieval.ts cannot be reused as-is: its arguments require a DbClient and repo closure, and its results identify repo entities.
findings.evidence: docs-retrieval.ts:103-131 `interface DocsRetrievalArgs { readonly db: DbClient; ... readonly closureRepos: readonly string[]; ... readonly kinds?: readonly ('document' | 'section' | 'config')[]; }`. findings.premise: Each story owns the catalog.json and release-install write path without overlap, and that path is covered by a shared contract.
findings.evidence: In the HLD, S004 owns "Basic validated bundled-package installation ... so retrieval is independently testable", and S005 owns "update staging, atomic publish/default switch, withdrawal overlays, recovery". The architecture section describes one catalog writer ("updates catalog by temporary-file fsync+atomic rename under a daemon serialized writer. Startup recovers valid orphan packages") but does not say which story owns it. No sc-contract defines the catalog file shape or the writer API: sc2 has only ReleaseAvailability.catalogGeneration, and sc6 only PublishRequest. S004 and S005 will therefore both write catalog.json, and S005 will either redesign S004's installer or depend on a private format. [files: docs/epics/di1-open-source-design-corpus-retrieval-E202610117e0ae92e/DEF.md]
findings.action: Assign the catalog layout and the serialized atomic writer, with its recovery, to one story, preferably S004 as part of basic install. Expose that writer as a shared contract that S005 extends for publish, setDefault and withdraw.

findings.premise: Corpus domain failures can be detected by IPC and MCP clients because they come back as a CorpusFailure discriminated union inside the result envelope, with explicit codes for disabled, unavailable-release, cursor-invalidated and degraded embedding.
findings.evidence: server.ts:193-197 passes a handler's returned value through as `result`, unchanged. Only a throw is flattened to a string. sc5 defines `CorpusResult<T> = { ok: true; value } | CorpusFailure` with codes 'invalid-input' | 'unavailable-release' | 'unsupported-schema' | 'cursor-invalidated' | 'corpus-disabled' | 'internal-error'. Degraded mode is reported as `status: 'degraded'` / `mode: 'lexical'`. The verification matrix checks that these codes survive the IPC and MCP round trip. [files: src/daemon/server.ts]

findings.premise: Every DEF acceptance criterion maps to a named test in the HLD verification matrix.
findings.evidence: The matrix lists S001/ac1 (publication rejection for missing provenance, examples, applicability or review), S001/ac2 (read round-trip), S002/ac1 (mixed-license import), S002/ac2 (notices enumeration), S003/ac1 (missing or gap coverage cell rejection), S003/ac2 (draft or inferred records excluded), S004/ac1 (platform and constraint fixtures over IPC/MCP), S004/ac2 (explicit gap and degraded mode), S005/ac1 (re-review and deprecation/withdrawal) and S005/ac2 (N+1 and rollback keep N evidence; tombstones). That is all ten DEF criteria. The plugin test command in vscode-plugin/package.json:775 (`tsx --test 'src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts'`) runs manifest-catalog.test.ts, so the s4 flag parity check is executed. [files: vscode-plugin/package.json]

summary.prose: Design knowledge ships as reviewed, versioned releases with traceable sources and reusable examples for Web, iOS and Android. Agents retrieve applicable guidance through insrc and keep exact evidence references. Updating the corpus never changes an approved project's choices.

body.frameworkSummary: Choose immutable release packages with a daemon-owned catalog and rebuildable retrieval indexes. Shared contracts below are proposed additions, not existing APIs. Corpus data is global public knowledge, independent of registered source repositories; DI2 owns project-private guideline storage and DI3 owns authoring workflows.
body.architectureShape:
Proposed domain location: src/design/corpus/ for contracts, validation, release installation and retrieval. Proposed adapter src/daemon/design-corpus-rpc.ts is composed into the existing handlers map in src/daemon/index.ts and served by src/daemon/server.ts; MCP adds a thin corpus query/read wrapper through IPC only. These paths except existing daemon files are new. Reuse existing LLMProvider/local embedder abstractions with sequential calls; any optional cloud editorial assistance uses CliProvider and critical role tiering. Normal retrieval needs no cloud generation. Existing src/analyze/docs-retrieval.ts is a ranking precedent, not a drop-in: its Args require DbClient/closureRepos and its results identify repo entities. Do not insert corpus records as fake repo entities or weaken repo.add.

Author eligible original/derived records and notices under proposed src/assets/design-corpus/. Existing copy-assets.mjs copies src/assets recursively to out/assets. Ship only a validated reviewed release, never candidate downloads. New PATHS.designCorpus points to ~/.insrc/design-corpus; daemon-owned filesystem packages are the canonical store, avoiding changes to code graph tables. Staging, immutable releases/<releaseId>, derived indexes/<releaseId>/<modelFingerprint>, catalog.json and append-only withdrawal events are distinct. JSON records have canonical sorted serialization and SHA-256 digests. Package digest covers sorted path+content hashes including notices, records, examples and review/coverage evidence, excluding only the self digest; a schema-versioned definition avoids hash ambiguity. Record ID is stable curator-assigned namespaced identity; recordVersion is content digest, not timestamp. Reject duplicate IDs, missing references, symlinks, path traversal, digest mismatch and unsupported schema before install.

Install verifies a bounded local staged package, fsyncs files and directory, atomically renames into immutable release directory, then updates catalog by temporary-file fsync+atomic rename under a daemon serialized writer. Startup recovers valid orphan packages and discards incomplete staging; catalog never references half-published content. Publish uses expected catalog generation and idempotency key; identical retry returns same release, conflicting retry fails. User-installed packages require explicit maintainer review metadata and local authorized install intent; hash integrity is not trust. No executing imported JS, shell or HTML. Original specimens are declarative data rendered safely; source imports are untrusted data and file-level eligibility remains an editorial gate.

A query resolves the requested release once (or current catalog default once), validates UI type, applies published/eligible/platform and hard structured constraints before scoring, and returns pinned record versions. For the seed corpus score all eligible records lexically; local embeddings may add exact semantic similarity across that same set. Reuse local embedding abstraction only after verifying input/model limits; chunk long records without truncation and aggregate with evidence links. Index keys include release, record digest, embedder model/version, dimensions and normalization version. Persisted indexes are disposable; rebuilding is serial and resumable. Embedding failure reports degraded lexical mode, never claims semantic completeness. Stable ordering uses score then record ID/version. Pagination freezes release and ranking/index version; changed availability invalidates cursor explicitly. A result limit affects presentation, not eligibility scanning, and reports total, truncated and nextCursor. No arbitrary silent corpus truncation. Rationale is a deterministic explanation of matched tags, constraints and source excerpts, not an invented design judgment. Conflicts and unsupported constraints are explicit gaps, not score penalties that allow unsafe recommendations.

Exact evidence lookup never falls forward to latest. Deprecated records remain readable with warnings but excluded from new default recommendations. Withdrawn references return a tombstone with reason and provenance identifiers; policy-blocked content is withheld even historically, while historical IDs/hashes/notices permitted to retain are preserved. Never silently rewrite a guideline or substitute newer content. DI2 persists sc1 references and its own approved decision snapshot; DI1 owns evidence availability. DI3 consumes query/read APIs and builds project-level guidelines, never page-specific guideline identities.

Digest dependency order (normative): compute recordVersion from canonical record content excluding recordVersion and review; review.contentDigest must equal that version. Compute candidateContentDigest over sorted record versions plus source, example and notice file hashes, excluding coverage/review envelopes and the manifest. Coverage refers only to recordId/recordVersion pairs, never final releaseId. After editorial review, compute reviewDigest over canonical coverage/review envelopes. Compute releaseId over the canonical manifest with releaseId omitted and all listed file hashes; the files list excludes the manifest itself. This prevents self-referential hashes while binding final release identity to review evidence. Change to content invalidates its review; publication requires exact digest matches and all coverage cells pass. Runtime EvidenceRef combines the resulting releaseId with a record pair.

Existing code evidence: s1 analyzer bundles locate daemon/index.ts, daemon/server.ts, db/search.ts and analyze/docs-retrieval.ts. Direct inspection supplements bounded graph discovery: docs-retrieval.ts:115 defines repo-scoped arguments, server.ts:187 dispatches the handlers map, copy-assets.mjs:28 copies assets/prompts, and shared/paths.ts:7 owns filesystem paths. All design/corpus paths, corpus IPC names, config keys and catalog/index layouts above are proposed new surfaces.

Review corrections: s4 adds designCorpus.enabled to src/config/config-catalog.ts as boolean, default false, main config domain, group Design intelligence; updates the relevant Config type and catalog row-count/shape assertions in src/config/__tests__/config-catalog-contract.test.ts. Existing src/config/reconcile.ts and reconcile-io.ts remain the catalog-driven integration; verify default fill, preservation and config.catalog settings exposure rather than adding a second settings registry. s5 consumes the same flag and does not introduce another. IPC clients receive the CorpusResult discriminated union inside the existing result envelope; the adapter normalizes validation/domain errors there because server.ts serializes thrown errors as strings. Maintainer mutation results use the same union with additional conflict and validation codes; no IPC envelope change is required.

Verification matrix for the approved DEF: S001/ac1 rejects omitted provenance/examples/applicability/review and domain-required payload; S001/ac2 read round-trip asserts stable identity, version, relationships, rationale and every source lineage field. S002/ac1 mixed eligible/unknown-license import admits only eligible bytes with exact revision, attribution and modifications; S002/ac2 release/export notices enumerate every included third-party asset. S003/ac1 publication rejects any missing domain/platform cell, gap cell or failed evaluation; human editorial review assesses quality of every passing cell. S003/ac2 draft generated/inferred records cannot enter published query or exact-read results; a reviewed inferred record remains labelled inferred, never source-authored. S004/ac1 platform/hard-constraint fixtures assert filtered results, caveats, fit and pinned evidence over real IPC serialization; invalid-input/unavailable-release/disabled results retain their codes after IPC and MCP round-trip. S004/ac2 no eligible match yields explicit gap, and unavailable semantic search reports degraded mode. S005/ac1 changed source/license requires a newly reviewed digest and tests deprecation/withdrawal overlays; S005/ac2 publishing N+1 and rollback leave N evidence unchanged, with withdrawal returning explicit tombstones and no substitution. Crash injection and concurrent/idempotent publication test durable visibility at every atomic boundary. All tests use temporary corpus directories and fake providers; opt-in live local embedding evaluation runs serially.

Settings mirrors (s4): add insrc.designCorpus.enabled to vscode-plugin/package.json under a Design intelligence configuration section, type boolean, default false, scope machine, with the same description as the catalog. Verify vscode-plugin/src/config/__tests__/manifest-catalog.test.ts exact key coverage, type/default/scope parity. No SettingsView.kt edit is needed: src/config/settings-catalog.ts derives groups from first-seen CONFIG_CATALOG order and JetBrains groupsOf consumes catalog.groups with fallback for unlisted groups. Verify that the catalog-driven boolean control renders and round-trips there. This is backend capability exposure in existing settings, not a separate project-design UI. Run both backend config contract tests and plugin manifest/settings checks when s4 implements the flag; no new IPC settings envelope is introduced.

Catalog ownership and atomicity (sc7): S004 owns catalog.json and the serialized writer/recovery for both initial install and later changes. Availability events are append-only entries within each atomic catalog snapshot, not a separate authoritative log requiring a cross-file transaction. Optional log exports are derived. S005 supplies validated mutations through sc7; it never edits catalog files. sc7 resolves availability-event precedence, checks release existence/schema and stage verification, rejects invalid defaults and generation conflicts, and atomically commits state plus idempotency receipt. An identical idempotency key/request digest returns its prior receipt before generation checking; a changed request under that key is a conflict. Recovering a complete orphan package registers it without selecting it as default or inferring publication approval; only a valid stored reviewed manifest may be installed. Recovered packages remain unavailable until that verification succeeds. Recovery never replays an uncommitted default or withdrawal intent. Tests inject crashes around rename/catalog commit and assert one authoritative generation, complete receipts, explicit tombstones and no unauthorized default change.

sharedContracts.name: Corpus record and pinned evidence identity
sharedContracts.purpose: Common immutable record, provenance and release identity across all stories and DI2/DI3.

sharedContracts.name: Release manifest and publication gate
sharedContracts.purpose: s1 establishes envelopes and gates used by import, curation, query and maintenance; s2 implements ingestion. Publication requires nonempty problem/tradeoffs, checks with explicit limits (or an explicit no-measurable-check rationale), and domainPayload.color/layout/style for corresponding color/layout/style records. Semantic roles and pairings must reference declared roles; examples and misuse examples must be present for every declared platform. Domain validation rejects an empty placeholder.

sharedContracts.name: File-level source eligibility and attribution
sharedContracts.purpose: Keep file licenses, exact upstream revisions and notices with every derived asset; repository license alone never admits content.

sharedContracts.name: Coverage and editorial review evidence
sharedContracts.purpose: Publication requires actual reviewed domain/platform combinations and content-bound review, not a record count.
sharedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface CoverageCell { domain: string; uiType: UiType; records: { recordId: string; recordVersion: string }[]; evaluationCases: string[]; status: 'pass' | 'gap'; reviewer: string; notes: string; }
interface CoverageReport { schemaVersion: 1; candidateContentDigest: string; cells: CoverageCell[]; crossPlatformCases: { id: string; status: 'pass' | 'fail'; evidence: string[] }[]; }

sharedContracts.name: Read-only corpus retrieval IPC
sharedContracts.purpose: DI3 searches reviewed public knowledge; DI2 resolves exact references. No project identity or guideline mutation is accepted.

sharedContracts.name: Release maintenance and withdrawal
sharedContracts.purpose: Stage verified updates with explicit publication, conflict detection and reversible default selection.

sharedContracts.name: Catalog persistence and atomic release writer
sharedContracts.purpose: S004 owns the sole catalog layout, atomic serialized writer and startup recovery. S005 invokes this contract for maintenance and never writes private catalog/index files.

storyBoundaries.internal: Own canonical schema, version/hash specification, publication validation interfaces and fixtures. This is the nearest ancestor for all shared identity/release contracts; storage and curator UI are not implied.
Own source adapters, local staging extraction, allowlist policy implementation and reproducible notices. Adapter specifics stay private; no unreviewed source contents enter published assets.

Own authored seed records, declarative specimens and reviewed coverage across ten domains and three UI types. A release names its maintainer/reviewer; unknown source sufficiency cannot be counted as coverage.

Own daemon package reader, catalog read adapter, deterministic filtering/ranking, local embedding cache, cursor implementation and thin MCP read tools. Keep ranking weights and cache format private and versioned. Basic validated bundled-package installation is included so retrieval is independently testable. Includes the single-sourced config-catalog entry, typed config exposure, settings/reconciliation verification and catalog contract-test update. Owns vscode-plugin/package.json setting mirror and verification of the unchanged catalog-driven JetBrains SettingsView.kt, validated by manifest/catalog parity and settings render/round-trip checks. Sole owner of catalog file layout, serialized atomic commit, receipts and recovery via sc7. Basic installation and maintenance use exactly this writer.

Own update staging, atomic publish/default switch, withdrawal overlays, recovery, release diffs and cross-release regression evaluation. Consume existing reader contracts; never change DI2 guideline state. Uses sc7 for all catalog/default/availability changes; owns upstream update policy and diff orchestration only, not a second writer or recovery implementation.

nonFunctional.performance: For a representative 1,000-record seed fixture, measure warm query p95 <=500 ms excluding local embedding inference; report embedding latency separately. This is a target, not a benchmark claim. If exceeded, optimize indexing without dropping eligible candidates; complete-result quality takes precedence. Cold index building is resumable and serial.
nonFunctional.security: Only eligible reviewed material is distributed. Validate all package paths and sizes, reject executable specimen content and remote includes; escape rendering. No arbitrary URL fetching at query time. Unknown hard constraints return gaps. Do not mix project-private data into the public corpus or embedding index.
nonFunctional.observability: Log release ID, query mode, eligible/matched counts, filter/gap reasons, index fingerprint and validation codes; avoid storing user query/brief text by default. Expose install/index health and explicit degraded retrieval, rather than silent fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Immutable package bytes plus atomic catalog and append-only availability events. Rebuild derived indexes on checksum/model mismatch. Inject crashes between each publication boundary; old release remains readable or a newly complete release becomes visible, never partial content. Retain pinned references across rollback; policy withdrawal returns tombstones.

phases.name: A — Record and release contracts
phases.rationale: Establish the shared schema and immutable identity rules first. Verify S001 publication rejection and complete metadata/lineage read round-trip.
phases.backwardCompat: No existing repo entity schema or registry behavior changes.

phases.name: B — Eligible source ingestion
phases.rationale: Prove eligibility, pinned-source extraction and notices against mixed-license fixtures.
phases.backwardCompat: Existing assets and build copy remain compatible; candidate downloads are excluded.

phases.name: C — Reviewed seed corpus
phases.rationale: Review each domain/platform cell and content-bound examples before distribution. Verify publication rejects gap/missing cells and draft or unreviewed inferred records are absent from published retrieval.
phases.backwardCompat: Existing runtime resources retain their layout; add a separate corpus asset subtree.

phases.name: D — Daemon retrieval pilot
phases.rationale: Expose read-only query, exact lookup and health with explicit gaps and degraded mode.
phases.backwardCompat: Additive IPC/MCP methods; existing search and repo registration unchanged. Disabled until a validated seed release is installed.

phases.name: E — Release maintenance
phases.rationale: Add update/diff/withdrawal, fault recovery and pinned-reference regression tests before enabling broad use.
phases.backwardCompat: Old release references remain resolvable or explicitly withdrawn; no implicit guideline edits.

rolloutOverview.orderingRationale: Matches approved s1→s2→s3→s4→s5 and every contract owner precedes consumers. DI2/DI3 consume published contracts without becoming DI1 story dependencies.

riskyBits.why: Repository license labels and record counts do not establish file reuse rights or usable native-mobile guidance.
riskyBits.mitigation: Require file-level manifests, named reviewers and all ten-domain/three-platform coverage cells; fill gaps with independently authored eligible guidance before release.

riskyBits.why: Mutable defaults, interrupted publication or license withdrawal can invalidate historical references.
riskyBits.mitigation: Immutable hashes, generation checks, atomic publish recovery and explicit tombstones; test N/N+1, rollback and withdrawal with DI2-compatible fixtures.

riskyBits.why: Repo search is not a drop-in corpus API; semantic service availability and platform conflicts affect recommendation quality.
riskyBits.mitigation: Use full eligible seed-set filtering/scoring, explicit unsupported constraints/degradation, reviewed positive/negative retrieval fixtures and model-versioned indexes.

alternativesConsidered.name: Versioned repository documentation
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Represent the corpus as registered repository documents and reuse document retrieval.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Maintain curated records and notices as documents in a corpus repository registered through repo.add. Existing document indexing and hybrid retrieval provide discovery.

Add release pins and eligibility metadata around indexed documents. Historical releases need distinct snapshots and explicit cross-repository access so project dependency closures do not accidentally hide or expose material.
pros: Reuses existing document indexing and search surfaces.
cons: Repo/entity identity and dependency-closure scoping do not directly represent global immutable corpus versions.
Document ranking does not enforce provenance or platform eligibility; dedicated gates remain necessary.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Generic retrieval is useful precedent but repo identity imposes unnecessary corpus coupling.

alternativesConsidered.name: Immutable release packages with daemon-owned catalog
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Publish content-addressed corpus packages and build isolated, disposable search indexes.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Curators publish validated immutable packages containing records, source manifest, notices, examples and coverage review. The daemon installs packages and owns their catalog, state overlay and retrieval; packages are independent of code repositories.

Use exact structured filtering and full eligible-record lexical scoring for the seed corpus, with local semantic ranking when available. Indexes are rebuildable derivatives keyed by release and model; every result resolves back to immutable evidence. Reuse daemon IPC and provider abstractions, while leaving repo entity storage unchanged.
pros: Release pins reproduce evidence without depending on repo registration.
Package validation and publication gates apply equally to records, notices and examples.
Index failure cannot rewrite source evidence or approved project decisions.
cons: Requires new corpus contracts, installation lifecycle and search adapter.
Semantic ranking quality requires evaluation and local embedding availability; degraded mode must be explicit.

alternativesConsidered.name: Database-first mutable corpus with revision history
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Author and query records directly in a dedicated daemon database with revision tables.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Store drafts, reviews, revisions and published records in a domain database with transactional release membership. Export packages as a secondary distribution surface.

All reads resolve release membership before ranking; publication snapshots are immutable despite mutable authoring records. The database becomes the authoritative recovery and migration boundary for both content and release history.
pros: Transactional authoring and release metadata share one owner.
Incremental curator edits do not require rebuilding an entire authoring package.
cons: Backup and migrations must preserve every historical record and bundled notice.
Adds a mutable authoring subsystem beyond the first release's curated dataset needs.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Feasible but adds mutable authoring/storage migration complexity without improving first-release design guidance.

citations.quotedText: Profiles locate daemon RPC modules and src/db graph/lance/search/doc-summaries. The stored DB import graph reports 159 incoming and 13 outgoing edges, with daemon/index.ts among importers; only 12 of 73 importing files are returned, and graph coverage is not established.
